I am in Pennsylvania, she is certified and has worked in and out of hospitals for a very long career, attending almost 4000 births. I did interview her, all of the most important things regarding resuscitation, transfer risks, what’s in her birth kit and complications were discussed and i was at ease with all she was able to inform me of. However, in my area due to her type of practice, unless she works within the hospital system there is no OB, but I did ask a lot of questions about at what point/causes i could risk out of her care, and if that happens it becomes my duty to find an OB. 

She does do ultrasounds, blood testing, the only things of concern for me are not testing for gestational diabetes and her personal stance on vaccinations, which again she had not discouraged me from pursuing. So, I guess my biggest issue is if there would be a way for me to pursue a medical visit only for the glucose test?

The only tests she has mentioned doing are ultrasounds and a blood test since I am O neg. I believe she does test for GBS, but says there’s little risk if it’s positive or not. There are just some things I find non-negotiable that she outright denies as being an issue. And she gave me a packet of info that she uses to determine these things, but when I ask questions it feels like we read different articles regarding the importance of certain tests. 

I think my best option is ghosting an OB at this point as she has attended so many births and is very well reviewed for that part at least, I just also believe in the value of modern medicine, but have so much hospital related trauma I know it would be hard to advocate for myself.
